name: Hoodsiderz
_comment_group: One more show under the Snapchat heading. The heading names the
network these frames are cut FOR and the channel is the show they are
cut from, so another show cutting for the same network is one more
folder under it rather than a heading of its own.
Like every channel under this heading it is a frame fetcher rather
than a thumbnail maker: a video goes in and a numbered grid of
vertical stills comes out, each captioned with what was being said
It is cut to Hall of Femme's design, and that pack is the one to read
first: the frame fetch, the vertical output, the transcription, the
rewrite, the card at the foot of the frame and every number in it are
the same and are named here rather than restated. What makes this show
itself is one sentence long - it is set in a hand instead of a
grotesque, on an orange card, in three colours the user pairs per
frame - and everything below is that sentence.
_comment_capture: The frame fetch, whole, from content/presets/snapchat-capture.json:
the slider's range, the 540x960 output, the transcription, and the
rewrite that turns it from speech into report. This channel has
nothing to say about any of it that its neighbours do not.
_comment_title: What separates this show from the others under the heading: it is set
in Chelsea Market Pro, on an orange card, in colours the user picks
per frame, with a picked word in Marydale Bold.
Everything else - the size, where the lines break, the capitals, the
shape of the card, where it stands on the frame, what a picked word
does - is the Snapchat caption design and is stated once, in
content/presets/snapchat-caption.json. This pack states only what
makes it this show, which is the whole of what a pack under this
A hand-lettered face is a thing a caption can only be set in because
of the card. Chelsea Market Pro is blocky and thick-stroked and holds
up at 40px, but its edges are drawn rather than ruled, and edges like
that are exactly what a photograph eats: over grain and detail the
letters read as texture rather than as words. On a solid ground
somebody chose, the hand is a voice instead of a risk - which is the
same argument Hall of Femme makes for its hairline, from the other end

_comment_color: Absolute white, and it is the channel's own answer - therefore what
every frame is set in until somebody presses a swatch, since a
frame stores no colour of its own until it is given one (see
state.textColorFor). It is one of the three in `colors` below, so
the white swatch is the one that shows as chosen on an untouched
frame; the swatch is found by matching this value rather than by
being listed first, which is why white sits second in a row that
White letters on the orange card is the pairing this show opens
on: the orange is the brand, so it is the CARD - the shape that is
a fifth of the frame and reads before anything on it - and the
type is what has to stay legible against it. The other eight
#FFFFFF and not an off-white, which matters here more than it would
on a dark card: an off-white on a mid-bright orange is a dirty
cream rather than a softened white, and there is nothing for a true
white to be too harsh against when the ground under it is a colour
_comment_colors: The three colours this show is set in, offered for the letters and
for the card behind them - three buttons each in the title panel
(see editor.renderColorButtons).
The same three in both lists and in one order, which is what every
pack under this heading does and for their reason: the point is the
PAIRING. Nine combinations of an orange, a white and a near-black,
and the ones worth having are the ones that read. A palette that
could only ever be used one way round would be a palette of three
cards, and this show's look is the pairing rather than any one of
them.
#0C0B0C is a near-black rather than #000000, and the difference is
worth the four characters. As a CARD it is a shape meant to look
printed onto the still rather than cut out of it - pure black on a
vertical video reads as a letterbox bar, something the player did,
and a hair of light in it keeps it a graphic. As TYPE it is ink,
and ink on an orange ground at caption size is easier on the eye a
few points off the floor.
Nothing stops the user setting white on white or black on black.
That is not an oversight: the two lists are independent because the
pairing is the feature, and a rule barring the three matching
combinations would cost the panel more explaining than an invisible
caption costs the user, who can see it is invisible and presses
another swatch.
`text` reaches the highlight as well as the block - see the note on
`colors` in js/channels.js. This channel's highlight is a different
HAND and not a different colour, so what colour the type is has one
answer and not two.
_comment_highlight: A picked word is set in Marydale Bold, in the same colour as the
rest of the block. Two hands on one line: the block is drawn with a
thick even marker, the picked word with a looser, thinner pen.
It is worth being plain about what that is and is not. Hall of
Femme picks words out by WEIGHT, 200 against 800 of one family, and
its picked word is unambiguously louder than its neighbours. Here
the picked word is LIGHTER than its neighbours despite being a face
called Bold - the two are different families, and Chelsea Market
Pro's Regular carries more ink than Marydale's Bold does. So this
is a change of VOICE rather than a change of volume: the word reads
as written by a different hand, an aside inside a sentence, which a
viewer sees immediately and which a shout is not what it makes.
Two measurements say it survives the setting. At the stated 40px
the two faces put their capitals within three pixels of each other,
so a picked word does not sit visibly small in the line it is part
of. And twelve capitals come out 306px wide in one face against 301
in the other, so which words are picked out does not move where the
lines break - worth knowing on a channel whose text arrives already
wrapped (see js/caption.js).
The colour it names is the block's, so the recolour draws exactly
what its neighbours are drawn in and the face is the whole of the
difference. Stated all the same, for the fallback reason `color`
above is stated - a highlight that changed colour as well as hand
would be two highlights.
The mode and the scope come from the preset, which is where the
argument for picking out words rather than lines lives.
_comment_panel: Orange, and the fill is the one thing about the card this pack
decides: its shape, its padding, its corners and its shadow are the
Snapchat caption design and come from the preset.
It is the first entry in `colors.panel` above as well, so the
swatch that shows as chosen on an untouched frame is the one at the
start of the row. Nothing requires that - the swatch is found by
matching this value rather than by being listed first - and the
type's own colour is deliberately NOT first in its row, which is
the same freedom used the other way round.

_comment_branding: No dark gradient. It exists to hold a title legible against the
photograph, and this title is not against the photograph at all - it
is on a card of its own. A scrim over every still would darken forty
pictures to solve a problem the card has already solved.
